Following reports of Israeli officials entering Mount Hermon, Syrian Ambassador Ibrahim Olabi told reporters, “Sovereignty is not selective. Territorial integrity is not negotiable.”

Ambassador Olabi told reporters that on the 9th of September 2026, “Israeli officials entered the sovereign territory of the Syrian Arab Republic and proceeded to the summit of Mount Hermon,” stressing that this action occurred amid the continued Israeli military presence and repeated incursions into Syrian territory.

He highlighted, “international law is clear. The Charter of the United Nations is clear. The 1974 Agreement on Disengagement between Syrian and Israeli Forces is equally clear.”

“Countries are here standing with Syria today to affirm that international law, the United Nations Charter, the United Nations Security Council resolutions and the established lines and arrangements under the 1974 Agreements must be fully respected and upheld,” the Syrian Ambassador emphasized.
Ambassador Olabi reiterated, “Syria's position has also been clear. It has consistently distanced itself from the ongoing regional escalation. It has repeatedly affirmed that it will not pose a threat to any of its neighbors. This responsible approach has been repeatedly acknowledged by members of the international community.”

He stressed, “any military, political or other action risks undermining the significant progress achieved by the Syrian government, progress that is vital to the international community and the Syrian people.”

Ambassador Olabi underscored, “countries here are standing with Syria today to reaffirm their unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.”

“In light of all the above, and particularly at this exceptionally volatile moment, Syria's sovereignty must be protected and its stability respected. This is for the sake of its people, the region and international peace and security,” the Syrian Ambassador concluded. | UN Web TV
